Discussion The SLB problem is inherently challenging due to the roundwise enforcement of constraints. Our works offers new, and refined insights into both the hardness of the problem through our instancedependent superlogarithmic lower bound, and to the effectiveness of doubly-optimistic methods for the same through our strong control on ET . In the process, we developed a new dual viewpoint of the SLB problem, by developing gaps for sets of constraints, which we believe is a conceptually important tool for such problems. Of course, a number of interesting questions remain open, e.g., are there computationally efficient ways to implement doubly-optimistic strategies for large U ; or if one can design methods that attain the strong safety guarantees of PO methods, but without making the strong assumptions of prior knowledge of safe points.
